```{r}

install.package(dplyr)
install.package(imager)
setwd()
library(reticulate) #package to access python libraries
use_python("C:/Windows/py.exe", required = T)
np <- import("numpy", convert = F)
library(dplyr)
labels <- read.csv("../data/styles.csv",
                     header= T) %>%
  unique(.)

#subset to 10,000 images. indexes are already random
labels <- labels[1:10000,]

images <- list.files("../data/images")
images  <- gsub(".jpg", "",images)
images <- images[images %in% labels$id]
#number of images is 9995. there are some photos not in label sheet

#get true labels
labels <- labels[labels$id %in% images,]

#get image paths again
images <- paste0("../data/images/",images, ".jpg")

library(imager)
photos <- lapply(images, load.image)
dim(photos[[1]]) #3 channels RGB #60h 80w 1d 3channels

summary(photos[[50]]) #not 8 bit pixelated, scale is 0 to 1

library(tensorflow)
library(keras3)

photos[[1]]
plot(photos[[1]])
plot(photos[[23]])

```


```{r label distribution}
summary(labels)

target_dist <- table(subset(labels,select=c(baseColour)))
#uneven distribution of colors
target_dist
tab <- data.frame(target_dist)
library(ggplot2)
target_plot <- ggplot(tab, aes(x= baseColour, y= Freq))+
  geom_col()+
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 0.5))+
  labs(title= "Target Color Label Distribution")
library(plotly)
ggplotly(target_plot)

table(subset(labels,select=c(gender))) #mostly women and men clothing
table(subset(labels,select=c(usage))) #mostly casual clothing


```

```{r data augmentation}
n_samples <- nrow(labels) #9995 photos
n_categories <- NROW(unique(labels$baseColour)) #46 colors

#weights to match up to majority class, majority class has lowest weight
weights <- n_samples / (n_samples * tab$Freq) #outputs weights for each class

#make a list for keras
class_weights <- vector()
for (i in 1:length(weights)) {
  class_index <- as.character(i - 1)
  #print(class_index)
  # Assign the weight to that specific class index
  class_weights[[class_index]] <- weights[i]
}

```
